findings.highlight: The town is unlively.
findings.evidenceJa: 町には活気がない
findings.governingReading: The town has no vitality.
findings.explanation: “Unlively” is nonstandard and weakens the opening atmospheric statement.

findings.highlight: devoid of any human presence
findings.evidenceJa: 人が住んでいる熱気さえも消えていた
findings.governingReading: Even the warmth or vitality showing that people live there has vanished.
findings.explanation: The English keeps absence of people but deletes the subtler disappearance of inhabited warmth.

findings.highlight: ever since I got to this hill
findings.evidenceJa: 坂道を登り始めてから
findings.governingReading: The arm begins hurting after Shirou starts climbing the slope.
findings.explanation: The English moves the onset from the act of climbing to arrival at the hill.

findings.highlight: Someone else’s arm is attached to me
findings.evidenceJa: 他所の腕を無理やりつけてる
findings.governingReading: Another person’s arm has been forcibly attached to him.
findings.explanation: The English omits the force of the transplant.

findings.highlight: I can’t get my breathing together.
findings.evidenceJa: 呼吸がなかなか整わない
findings.governingReading: His breathing will not readily settle.
findings.explanation: “Get my breathing together” is malformed English.

findings.highlight: When it gets hotter than my normal temperature
findings.evidenceJa: 平熱を大きく逸脱した瞬間
findings.governingReading: The stabbing pain begins the instant the arm greatly departs from normal body temperature.
findings.explanation: The English removes the magnitude and precise threshold.

findings.highlight: pain attacks my chest from my arm
findings.evidenceJa: ズシャ、と肩口から胸に痛みが突き刺さる
findings.governingReading: With a sudden stabbing onset, pain pierces from the shoulder into the chest.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the onset sound and replaces the shoulder-to-chest path with generic arm-to-chest pain.

findings.highlight: where the pain is coming from
findings.evidenceJa: 痛みの仕組みがどんなモノなのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks he has roughly understood the mechanism of the pain.
findings.explanation: The English reduces a causal mechanism to the pain’s location or source.

findings.highlight: When it overheats
findings.evidenceJa: 左腕の中で溜まりきって一杯になった時
findings.governingReading: Heat accumulates inside the arm until it is completely full.
findings.explanation: “Overheats” deletes the capacity model governing how excess heat enters his body.

findings.highlight: my stomach torn by Berserker
findings.evidenceJa: 腹を根こそぎ持っていかれた
findings.governingReading: Berserker once tore away Shirou’s abdomen wholesale, down to the roots.
findings.explanation: The English narrows abdomen to stomach and weakens wholesale removal to tearing.

findings.highlight: my ribs crushed by Rider
findings.evidenceJa: ライダーに肋を砕かれかけた
findings.governingReading: Rider nearly crushed his ribs.
findings.explanation: The English changes a near outcome into completed crushing.

findings.highlight: getting stabbed by my own body
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の腕に自分の体が“貫かれる”
findings.governingReading: His own body is “pierced” by his own arm.
findings.explanation: The English makes his body the weapon rather than the arm piercing it.

findings.highlight: go home and see Sakura while I still look well
findings.evidenceJa: 元気な姿で、桜にただいまを言わないと
findings.governingReading: Shirou must return promptly in a healthy-looking state and say “I’m home” to Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the homecoming greeting and adds that his healthy appearance is only temporarily retained.

findings.highlight: I want to rest for today.
findings.evidenceJa: 今は体を休めたい
findings.governingReading: For now, Shirou wants to rest his body.
findings.explanation: The English changes the object and temporal scope into resting for the remainder of the day.

findings.highlight: says something with difficulty
findings.evidenceJa: たどたどしい言葉遣いで
findings.governingReading: Sakura speaks in a halting, faltering manner.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the kind of difficulty unspecified and loses her audible delivery.

findings.highlight: You can’t even move the fingers
findings.evidenceJa: 指先だって満足に動かない
findings.governingReading: The fingertips do not move properly or adequately.
findings.explanation: The English turns severe limitation into absolute inability and broadens fingertips to whole fingers.

findings.highlight: because it’s meaningless
findings.evidenceJa: わたしに話しても無駄だから
findings.governingReading: Sakura asks whether he stays silent because telling her would be pointless.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the act of telling and Sakura as its recipient.

findings.highlight: My insensitivity leaves me speechless.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の馬鹿さかげんに言葉を失う
findings.governingReading: Shirou is struck speechless by the extent of his own foolishness.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes one specific moral flaw, insensitivity, for his broader self-condemnation.

findings.highlight: you’re right, but you’re wrong
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の言う通りだけど違う
findings.governingReading: Shirou says Sakura is right, but that is not what his reaction means.
findings.explanation: The English turns correction of her inference into the direct contradiction that she is both right and wrong.

findings.highlight: not good to bluff
findings.evidenceJa: 強がるのはよくない
findings.governingReading: Shirou admits it is wrong to put on a brave or tough front.
findings.explanation: “Bluff” suggests calculated deception or an empty threat rather than emotional posturing.

findings.highlight: don’t tell Sakura about it so she doesn’t get worried?
findings.evidenceJa: なにが桜を不安にさせたくないから黙っていよう、だ
findings.governingReading: Shirou scornfully quotes his own excuse: “What was that about keeping quiet so Sakura would not worry?”
findings.explanation: The English becomes a fresh instruction not to tell Sakura, reversing the retrospective self-rebuke.

findings.highlight: My arm turned out fine
findings.evidenceJa: 腕はなんとかなった
findings.governingReading: Shirou says something was managed regarding the arm, despite its severe state.
findings.explanation: “Turned out fine” contradicts the arm’s established immobility and pain.

findings.highlight: you looked really good
findings.evidenceJa: すごくカッコ良かったです
findings.governingReading: Without having seen the event, Sakura insists Shirou must have been extremely admirable or heroic.
findings.explanation: “Looked really good” shifts praise toward witnessed appearance and physical attractiveness.

findings.highlight: I couldn’t save Illya like I’d planned
findings.evidenceJa: 満足にイリヤも助けられなかった
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he could not rescue Illya adequately.
findings.explanation: The English invents deviation from a plan and risks suggesting the rescue itself failed.

findings.highlight: being alive is good enough
findings.evidenceJa: 生きてるだけで合格点
findings.governingReading: Merely returning alive earns a passing grade.
findings.explanation: The English preserves adequacy but deletes the school-test metaphor.

findings.highlight: You’re good-looking.
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩はかっこいいです
findings.governingReading: Sakura calls Shirou admirable or cool.
findings.explanation: The English narrows her praise to physical attractiveness.

findings.highlight: Sakura must have cheered up
findings.evidenceJa: 物凄く機嫌が直ったのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether Sakura’s mood has improved tremendously.
findings.explanation: “Must have” promotes his tentative reading toward certainty.

findings.highlight: say something like that with a big smile
findings.evidenceJa: とんでもないコトを満面の笑顔で言う
findings.governingReading: Sakura says something outrageous with a smile covering her whole face.
findings.explanation: The English removes the outrageousness and weakens the full-faced smile.

findings.highlight: both jump back at the same time
findings.evidenceJa: 同時に半歩後退して
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Sakura retreat exactly half a step together.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the small synchronized recoil with a jump.

findings.highlight: the two of you having a lovers’ quarrel
findings.evidenceJa: 二人して仲良くケンカしてる
findings.governingReading: Rin finds the two affectionately or harmoniously quarrelling together.
findings.explanation: The English invents an explicitly romantic category for the domestic bickering.

findings.highlight: a large bag
findings.evidenceJa: 大きなボストンバッグ
findings.governingReading: Rin puts down a large Boston or travel bag at the entrance.
findings.explanation: The English drops the object type that signals moving in.

findings.highlight: Illya, silently radiating a strange pressure
findings.evidenceJa: 妙な緊迫感で押し黙ったイリヤ
findings.governingReading: Illya stands silent in an oddly tense state.
findings.explanation: The English makes Illya project an intimidating pressure rather than experience tension.

findings.highlight: I’m going to stay over here
findings.evidenceJa: 今夜からここで生活して
findings.governingReading: Rin announces that she will live in the house starting tonight.
findings.explanation: “Stay over” suggests a short visit and loses the stated starting point.

findings.highlight: It’ll be hard work if I want him to become strong in a short time.
findings.evidenceJa: 短期間で戦力になってもらうにはスパルタしかない
findings.governingReading: Rin says Spartan treatment is the only way to make Shirou combat-capable quickly.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the only-option claim and combat readiness, replacing them with generic hard work and strength.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka Rin sets a schedule even I haven’t heard about.
findings.evidenceJa: しれっと、俺ですら聞いた事のないスケジュールを口にする
findings.governingReading: Rin casually and brazenly announces a schedule even Shirou has never heard.
findings.explanation: The English preserves surprise but drops Rin’s unruffled delivery.

findings.highlight: you’ll make meals for me
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと三食付きにして
findings.governingReading: Rin demands that the lodging properly include three meals a day.
findings.explanation: The English omits the concrete three-meal term of her mock debt collection.

findings.highlight: I want to object
findings.evidenceJa: ところどころ反論したい
findings.governingReading: Shirou wants to object to parts of Rin’s account.
findings.explanation: The English makes his objection general and loses his admission that much of it is true.

findings.highlight: I understand
findings.evidenceJa: 納得します
findings.governingReading: Sakura says she will accept or be persuaded because Shirou asks.
findings.explanation: The English weakens reluctant consent into cognitive understanding.
